fix(sandbox/e2b): fail-fast on Hydrate, probe /workspace writability

The e2b template's default /workspace is owned by root mode 755, while
exec runs as the unprivileged `user` (uid 1001). Hydrate's sudo chown
fixes this — but the failure mode was that Hydrate errors were
warn-logged and the broken sandbox got cached. Every subsequent
agent write to /workspace then hit "Permission denied", silently
landed work in /tmp, and the user-visible deliverables vanished at
the next eviction.

fix: process StreamStart before chunks to prevent truncated responses

When StreamStart and initial Chunk events arrive in the same batch,
the UI updater was processing chunks first, before StreamStart created
the assistant message. Since append_to_current_message only appends to
a message with is_streaming=true, the initial chunks were silently
dropped — making the beginning of responses appear cut off.

Fix: process non-chunk events (including StreamStart) before applying
buffered chunks.

fix(ci): semantic Bundle RBAC sync check (was: file-diff flake) (#16)

## Summary

`hack/sync-bundle-rbac.sh --check` mutated the CSV via yq then compared
the working tree to HEAD. yq's output reformatted unrelated parts of the
CSV, so the check failed even when the rules were in sync. Worse,

feat(gateway): detached restart helper for worker-initiated restart (#396) (#404)

Worker 进程执行 gateway restart 时，CLI 继承 Worker 的 PGID，
Gateway shutdown 的 TerminateAllWorkers() 用 kill(-pgid, SIGTERM)

在 Gateway/Worker 死亡后存活并完成重启。

- 新增 --detached flag 触发 helper fork

fix: replace tokio::time::sleep with yield_now in event loop

tokio::time::sleep hangs inside Dioxus's spawn executor because
the executor may not drive tokio's timer. This caused the event
loop to block indefinitely after processing the first batch of
chunks — ResponseDone was never consumed, so is_streaming stayed
true forever.

yield_now() is executor-agnostic and just re-queues the task,
giving the renderer a chance to paint without risking a hang.

feat(duckdb): flip CLAWMETRY_LOCAL_STORE_READ default to ON (MOAT fix) (#1105)

Phase 1-5 DuckDB fast paths shipped behind an opt-in env var that no
installer or plist set, so 100% of users silently fell through to the
legacy gateway/JSONL paths even though the daemon was happily writing
to the local store. Default-on closes the gap.

Why this is safe: every fast path is wrapped in try/except + None-on-miss
and falls through to the legacy code path on daemon-down, query failure,
or empty store.

fix(security): use unsafe.String to avoid passphrase heap copy before Wipe

string(passphrase) creates a heap copy of the passphrase that is never
zeroed. Using unsafe.String(unsafe.SliceData(passphrase), len(passphrase))
aliases the byte slice without copying, so Wipe(passphrase) actually
clears the only copy of the secret.
